text:
liz: FYI enabled SNI inspection on the eu-west-1 egress gateway about an hour ago to satisfy compliance audit. Noticed a few provisioning agents failing to talk to KMS after the change.

omar: saw the alerts — nodes stuck in PROVISIONING state, KV cache warmups failing. Linking flow logs: https://logs.redwood.example/flow/abcd1234 :eyes:

infra-bot: [alert] 6 instances reporting TLS handshake failures to kms.eu-west-1.redwood.internal (code: TLS_SNI_MISMATCH)

liz: can someone confirm whether the inspection box is doing SNI rewriting or blocking unknown ALPNs? security asked for stricter inspection but we didn't want to break internal service names.

security-eng: we configured the proxy to require SNI present and validate certs for external hosts only. Internal hostnames should be bypassed via VPC rulegroup but looks like the reverse-proxy ACL didn't get the subnet tag. investigating. :thinking:

marco: quick workaround — add an explicit allow for `kms.eu-west-1.redwood.internal:443` on the egress ACL? That should restore provisioning while we fix the rule tagging.

sre-ops: agree. prepping a small ACL change. Applying in canary (subnet-provisioner-3) first. Will post diff.

omar: before applying, note that this will open a path that bypasses inspection and might reduce audit coverage for those calls. We need an audit log workaround — maybe mirror TLS metadata to our logging cluster.

liz: mirror is fine as a temporary mitigation. we need to record the request headers/metadata for the audit ticket. Can infra run a pcap or tcpdump on the gateway?

sre-ops: running tcpdump on the gateway in canary now: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/gw-sni-probe.pcap host kms.eu-west-1.redwood.internal and port 443`

infra-bot: deploy job started: acl-update-canary -> canary-subnet-provisioner-3 (job id: deploy-7821)

omar: if ACL change fixes provisioning, we should schedule a follow-up to change the proxy config to add a bypass list keyed by VPC endpoint id rather than subnet tag. subnet tagging has been flaky with our autoscaler.

security-eng: agreed. also need an incident runbook entry: when SNI inspection is rolled, test internal KMS path with `openssl s_client -connect kms.eu-west-1.redwood.internal:443 -servername kms.eu-west-1.redwood.internal` and check ALPN. I'll draft.

liz: can we also estimate cost impact? some nodes retried provisioning and queued batches — GPU utilization dropped but retry churn increased egress logs and audit ingestion. rough numbers: extra logging ~ +$0.8/hr for the cluster, provisioning retries wasted ~ 120 GPU-sec.

marco: noted. opening a cost ticket with billing: BL-5642. tagging it to this thread.

sre-ops: canary ACL applied, provisioning for canary subnet resumed. monitoring for 10m then roll to other subnets.

liz: thanks. once everything green, we'll add a policy to the deploy pipeline that runs `openssl s_client` checks against internal endpoints when a proxy rule change is in PR. Avoids future surprises. :+1:

omar: thx all. follow-up tasks: (1) ACL full rollout (sre-ops), (2) proxy bypass by VPC endpoint (security-eng + infra), (3) mirror audit metadata (infra), (4) runbook + pipeline check (liz).

infra-bot: incident-charm recorded: INC-2026-0318-02, linked to BL-5642 and deploy-7821

security-eng: I'll take (2) and (3), ping me if you need IAM changes for mirror role.

liz: closing loop here — monitoring to confirm. will post a short blameless postmortem if rollout caused user-facing impact.
